canada.summary: Police believe Scot MacDermid may have left or will try to leave Canada, and are working with Interpol to find him and the children: nine-year-old Lesley and six-year-old George.

canada.summary: Students will be back in class Monday in Fort Simpson, N.W.T., after education officials said a pest control company found no more bedbugs in the local schools. The schools were closed all week after staff saw bedbugs fall from someone's belongings at the school.

canada.title: Religious health-care facilities can continue to ban MAID on site, B.C. Supreme Court rules
canada.summary: The B.C. Supreme Court has upheld the exemption that allows religious health-care facilities to prohibit medical assistance in dying. The decision means facilities such as Vancouver’s St. Paul’s Hospital can continue to require patients that want MAID to transfer to another facility.

canada.title: No sticker shock at little libraries filled with toy cars outside Winnipeg homes
canada.summary: Two Winnipeggers built Hot Wheels libraries in their front yards for neighbourhood kids to enjoy. The two don't know each other, and it's a coincidence that they decided to build them at the same time.

canada.title: What time is it? Ask the Beaverbrook Art Gallery's 24-hour movie exhibit
canada.summary: The 24-hour video installation by Swiss-American artist Christian Marclay is now at the Fredericton gallery. It's made of about 12,000 clips from movies and TV shows, each one showing or mentioning a time, and it plays in sync with the real time of day.

canada.summary: A new $6.5-billion federal forestry strategy to modernize the industry means funding opportunities for New Brunswick businesses, officials say. Exactly how much, though, is unclear.

lines: Good evening. I’m Hannah Thibedeau, and this is your Palindrome News brief.

The Supreme Court of Canada has upheld Quebec’s secularism law and its use of the notwithstanding clause – as Saskatchewan waits to have its own case heard in the new year, The Canadian Press reports.

The federal government on Friday prioritized construction of a critical road in the Northwest Territories by designating the Mackenzie Valley Highway as a project of national interest, The Canadian Press reports.
A First Nation in northern Manitoba has declared a state of emergency over what it says is unsafe drinking water.
iRestore’s Black Friday sale cuts up to 58% off LED face masks and hair growth helmets, with savings of up to $470 on select light therapy devices, Fox News reports.
Kenneth Law apologizes in court to victims’ families as Crown seeks 25-year sentence, The Canadian Press reports.
OpenAI sued Apple on Friday, accusing the Big Tech giant of stealing its trade secrets and blocking its access to hardware suppliers, Reuters reports.
That’s your brief. We’ll keep watching, so you don’t have to.
